# Imports
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
# import libraries
library(cowplot)
library(glue)
library(pracma)
library(reshape)
library(scales)
library(truncnorm)
```
A researcher hypothesizes that TV stimulation for kids will result in a decrease in the number of pieces of candy corn eaten. The kids are subjected to 5 hours of television. The number of candy corn candies consumed during a 10-minute period is counted both with and without TV. 

Compute the appropriate t-test for the data provided below.

With TV	Without TV
12	8
7	7
3	4
11	14
8	6
5	7
14	12
7	5
9	5
10	8

```{r}
# Make two vectors with different columns
with_tv <- c(12, 7, 3, 11, 8, 5, 14, 7, 9, 10)
without_tv <- c(8, 7, 4, 14, 6, 7, 12, 5, 5, 8)

# Run a paired t-test
t.test(with_tv, without_tv, paired = TRUE)
```


What is your computed answer for the following, based on the date in the table above?
Mean =	Mean =
S =	S =
S2 =	S2 =
```{r}
mean(with_tv)
mean(without_tv)

sd(with_tv)
sd(without_tv)

var(with_tv)
var(without_tv)
```

What is your computed t-test answer?

```{r}
t.test(with_tv, without_tv, paired = TRUE)
```

What is the null hypothesis in this study?

```{r}
cat("The null hypothesis in this study is that TV does not impact the number of candy corn eaten.")
```

What is the alternate hypothesis?

```{r}
cat("The alternative hypothesis in this study is that TV does make a difference on the number of candy corn eaten.")
```
What probability level did you choose and why?

```{r}
cat("The probability level we are using is alpha = 0.05. This means we're willing to accept a 5% chance of incorrectly rejecting null hypothesis, which is a standard value. Low alpha such as 0.01 would make it harder to detect real effects where as a alpha such as 0.1 would increase the risk of false positives.")
```

What are your degrees of freedom?

```{r}
cat("Degrees of freedom follows this formula: df = n - 1. Since we have 10 rows, our df would be 10-1. Therefore our degrees of freedom is 9.")
```


Is there a significant difference between the two testing conditions? Interpret your answer.

```{r}
# Just to test again
t.test(with_tv, without_tv, paired = TRUE)

cat("There is no statistically significant difference between the number of candy corn eaten with TV stimulation and without it (p = 0.2208 > 0.05). This means we fail to reject the null hypothesis. In this sample, watching TV does not appear to significantly affect candy corn consumption.")
```
